title: Tournament Management
subtitle: From first draw to final result — everything an organiser touches.

hero.alt: A tournament overview with the settings pills across the top

intro: Every tournament in TournaQ opens on the same screen: how far along you are, and a row of pills carrying every setting the event runs on — teams, players, courts, format, seeding, finish time.

Those pills are not labels. Each one opens the sheet that changes it, right up until play starts and the setting locks. This page is what sits behind each of them, and what happens to a tournament after the last match.
bestfor: Organisers setting an event up and adjusting it once it is running
Anyone who has had to rebuild a schedule because one thing changed
Clubs running the same event repeatedly

sections.title: The settings row
sections.text: The pills across the top of a tournament are the controls. A pencil means it can still be changed; a padlock means play has started and it cannot.

cards.p: Who is in the event, and which players make up each team. Add a team, drop one, or fix a name that was typed wrong at registration.
cards.alt: The teams sheet listing every team in the tournament

cards.p: The order teams enter the draw, which decides who meets whom and how late the strongest teams collide. Seed by hand or leave it as entered.
cards.alt: The seeding sheet setting the order teams enter the draw

cards.p: How many courts the event has to play with. Change it mid-event and the schedule redistributes rather than breaking.
cards.alt: The court count sheet for changing how many courts the event uses

cards.p: Points target, sets, and the shape of a match. Set once for the event so every scorecard opens with the right rules.
cards.alt: The game format sheet setting the points target and match shape

cards.p: The fixture list the current settings would produce, before anyone plays. If it does not fit the day, change the courts or the match length and look again.
cards.alt: A preview of the generated schedule before the tournament is created

cards.p: Once results exist, changing the team count or the format would invalidate them. TournaQ says so rather than silently corrupting a half-played event.
cards.alt: A dialog explaining why a locked setting cannot be changed once play has started

sections.title: Courts and allocation
sections.text: Multi-court events live or die on who is where. TournaQ assigns the courts and shows you the whole plan on one screen.

cards.p: Every round against every court, so the shape of the day is visible at a glance — including the team that has been given the far court three times running.
cards.alt: A grid of rounds against courts showing which teams are assigned where

cards.p: Courts can be named and taken in or out of use, which matters when one has the sun in your eyes or the club wants it back at four.
cards.alt: The court settings sheet for naming and managing courts

cards.p: Tap any match for its teams, court, time slot and referee — and to reassign any of them without leaving the screen.
cards.alt: A match detail sheet showing teams, court, time slot and referee

sections.title: Getting results in
sections.text: Not every match is scored live on the phone that owns the tournament. Both of the other routes are supported rather than tolerated.

cards.p: Type the final score into the match card and the standings, brackets and tables update exactly as if the scorecard had been used. This is how a tournament survives a court that ran ahead while you were refereeing another.
cards.alt: A dialog for entering a final score without opening the scorecard

cards.h: Or take one from another phone
cards.p: A scorecard scored on a second device arrives marked as imported, so an event run across several phones can be folded back into one without anyone retyping scores.
cards.alt: A scorecard that arrived from another device, marked as imported

sections.title: Off the phone and back again
sections.text: A tournament lives on the device that runs it, and nothing needs a signal. There are two ways out: a spreadsheet for the whole event, or a QR code for one match.

cards.h: The whole event, as a spreadsheet
cards.p: Export writes a real .xlsx — schedule, teams and results, one row per match. Watch the event from a laptop, fill in scores away from the phone, then import the file back. TournaQ reports what it recorded, replaced and skipped rather than applying it silently.
cards.alt: The tournament menu offering Import result, Export tournament and Import tournament

cards.p: Every match card carries a QR button. Show the code on one phone, scan it on another, and the scorecard travels between them — no reception, no account, nothing uploaded.
cards.alt: A QR code sheet for handing a single scorecard to another device

cards.p: When an import would replace results already recorded, TournaQ shows what is about to change and asks first.
cards.alt: A confirmation showing which existing results an import would replace

sections.title: Running it again
sections.text: The event you run every month should not need rebuilding every month.

cards.p: Duplicate a finished event and you get its settings, courts and format as a fresh one, ready for a new set of teams. The monthly open takes a minute instead of a rebuild.
cards.alt: The copy tournament sheet, duplicating an event as a template for the next one

cards.p: Results that arrived from other devices sit on their own tab in the hub, next to your own history, so it stays obvious which were scored here and which were not.
cards.alt: A mode hub with an Imported tab beside the tournament history
